source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Changing on a regular schedule and assessing skin at each change, rather than leaving the wafer in place as long as possible as the new caregiver is currently suggesting","B":"Avoiding any assessment of the peristomal skin during changes, which is not the appropriate approach to this particular aspect of ostomy care","C":"Changing as infrequently as possible to conserve supplies, similar to what the new caregiver is currently suggesting for this client's ostomy care","D":"Using the same barrier wafer indefinitely without replacing it, similar to what the new caregiver is currently suggesting for this client"}}
source_row.rationale: Best practice for ostomy pouching system changes includes changing the system on a regular schedule (following product-specific guidance and the individual client's needs) or promptly if leakage occurs, while gently cleansing and thoroughly assessing the peristomal skin at each change for any signs of irritation or breakdown, supporting both stoma/skin health and pouch adhesion/security.
